adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3 — belongs_to :category` has no existence/required validation and the migration adds no foreign key, so a host row can end up pointing at a `category_id` for a category that is later deleted (or was never valid); `record_for_host` will keep returning that row and `TopicEmbed.import` will hand PostCreator a dangling `category_id`, silently routing new embedded topics into a non-existent category instead of failing or falling back safely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with `belongs_to :category` but no `validates :category, presence: true` / existence check, and the migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` without adding a foreign key constraint. Additionally, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `category_id` directly from params (or uncategorized if blank) without verifying the category exists. Since there’s no FK, an `embeddable_hosts` row can end up with a `category_id` that doesn’t correspond to an actual category (e.g., stale after category deletion or via bad input). `TopicEmbed.import` then uses `eh.try(:category_id)` when creating posts, so an invalid/stale id can propagate into newly created embedded topics rather than being prevented at the DB/model layer. Whether PostCreator later raises vs. accepts the dangling id depends on code not shown, but the underlying referential-integrity problem is real and introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — Broadening the shared, globally-invoked `_hydrateEmbedded` regex to match any `*_ids` key means every future serializer that opts into `rest_serializer: true` will have any raw id-array field (e.g. `tag_ids`, `group_ids`, `moderator_ids`) silently renamed/replaced instead of left as-is, with no per-field opt-in or allowlist to scope the new behavior to the embedding feature

app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` produces the `embeddable_host_ids` + side-loaded `embeddable_hosts` shape that only exists to exercise the newly broadened global store.js hydration path — a single narrow feature is driving a blanket, unscoped change to a shared data-layer contract used by every model in the app instead of a locally-scoped hydration mechanism

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — hydrated || []` is dead code since `Array.prototype.map` always returns a (truthy) array even when empty, giving a false impression of a null/undefined guard on the new plural hydration path

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural hydration branch, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array object if it runs, and arrays are truthy even when empty. Therefore `hydrated || []` is redundant/dead. However, this does not introduce a functional bug by itself (and it also does not actually guard against `obj[k]` being null/undefined, since `.map` would throw before the `|| []` could matter). This is best characterized as a minor redundancy/style nit rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore, so `basePath` would misclassify any admin model type name containing more than one underscore as non-admin

adjudication.rationale: The new `basePath` logic uses `type.replace('_', '-')`, which indeed only replaces the first underscore. However, in this diff the only admin model types involved are `plugin`, `site-customization` (matching `site_customization` with a single underscore), and `embeddable-host` (matching `embeddable_host` with a single underscore). There is no admin model name in `ADMIN_MODELS` here that contains more than one underscore, so no misclassification is introduced by this change as shown in the diff; the finding is a hypothetical future-proofing concern rather than a verifiable defect in the current patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9 — execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError/IndexError and hard-crashes the migration if no category name matches the `embed_category` site setting value (e.g. zero rows returned).
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the migration calling execute(...)[0]['id'] without ensuring the SQL query returned any rows, causing a hard crash (NoMethodError/IndexError) when the embed_category setting yields no matching category/row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — Fallback lookup `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id` will raise and abort the migration if that site_settings row is missing or was already removed.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` would indeed raise if that query returned zero rows. However, nothing in this diff removes `uncategorized_category_id` (the migration only deletes `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category`), and Discourse relies on `uncategorized_category_id` being a core site setting that should exist. So the finding hinges on an unproven external condition (missing core row) rather than a defect introduced/observable in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Host values from the free-text `embeddable_hosts` site setting are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT string without escaping, so any stored host containing a single quote breaks the SQL or corrupts the insert.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting, splits it into lines (`records.each do |h|`), and then does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL string with no escaping/quoting helper, any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will produce invalid SQL or alter the statement. This is a concrete correctness/safety issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Migration has no `down`/reversible path and unconditionally deletes the original `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` site_settings rows after a raw-SQL backfill, making the change irreversible with no way to recover pre-migration config if the backfill was wrong.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` is defined using `def change`, but it performs multiple `execute` calls (including inserts and a final `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`). Raw `execute` statements are not automatically reversible in Rails, and there is no `down` method or `reversible` block to restore the deleted `site_settings` rows. As a result, rolling back this migration will be impossible (Rails will treat it as irreversible) and the original config values are permanently deleted after the backfill, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Backfilled host values are inserted as-is without lowercasing or deduplication, but runtime lookups use `lower(host)`, so previously-working embeds with mixed-case hosts can silently stop matching after migration.

adjudication.rationale:
The migration inserts the prior `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values verbatim, but the proposed issue about *mixed-case* hosts is not supported by the new lookup logic. Runtime matching uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so a stored value like `EvilTrout.com` will still match a lookup of `eviltrout.com` (case is normalized on the DB side via `lower(host)`). Therefore, mixed-case entries would not “silently stop matching” due to lowercasing.

(There is a different potential issue: the migration bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths, so stored values containing schemes/paths could fail to match later. But that’s not what the finding claims.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table (and its data) before recreating it, which is destructive if this migration is ever re-run or the table was manually created earlier.

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. That is inherently destructive behavior if the table exists for any reason (e.g., migration re-run, partial deploy, manual creation), and the diff shows this option is unnecessary for a normal first-time migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` patches a naming mismatch between Rails snake_case and Ember dasherized model names at one call site instead of normalizing the type once at the boundary, and only replaces the first underscore so it silently fails for any future multi-word model name

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only relevant admin model added is `embeddable-host`, and the corresponding snake_case form would be `embeddable_host` (a single underscore). `type.replace('_', '-')` correctly handles that. The claim that it “silently fails for any future multi-word model name” relies on hypothetical types with multiple underscores; no such type is introduced or used in this diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect here. The “normalize once at the boundary” point is architectural/style rather than a concrete bug evidenced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:1 — ADMIN_MODELS is a hardcoded whitelist array that every new admin model must remember to append to, growing as an ad-hoc list rather than being derived from a naming convention or adapter metadata

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a hardcoded `ADMIN_MODELS` array in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6`, and this change appends `'embeddable-host'` to it to make the new admin model route under `/admin/`. However, this is an existing design choice (not newly introduced as a defect here) and the change correctly updates the list to support the new model. The finding is a general maintainability/architecture critique rather than a concrete bug/correctness/security problem verifiable from the diff.
